why: when a key was pinned and when an offer came, and the moment a lasting change is judged at (with mono and the boot, pending.ts): labels, and an offer's hour, where the admin's yes against the fingerprint is the gate
the time label in controlNow's wall: control.json's since and the op's times, for people to read. A forced deadline is on this boot's mono (forceAt), and the break-glass stop's wait is counted
days until a date and recent logins: display
how long ago the loop's last request and beat were: rows that say OK with a time; the power log's last 30 days, a WARN only; when a lasting change lapses, with mono and the boot beside it
the hour the GitHub key keeper's counts are kept under, and GitHub's Date against the box's for the clock guard: display and a reason
the guard's and the workspaces state's freshness (a stale read FAILs, so a step fails closed) and how recent a loss or a moved log is: display
the answers envelope's at, for a usage error, a rename and every answer: a label; a streamed line's at: a label
the real Clock itself: every other read goes through it or Sys

the id of the declined event, made before the admin's entry that names it: a label; and the moment the waiting changes are judged at, by the box's boot and monotonic clock as well, so a step either way lapses an item, never keeps one
when the connect op began, and how long the listener may live inside the op's deadline: the op's record and GitHub's created_at decide

moved from cli.ts: the load session's wanted read and the workspaces hold's freshness for the loop, which fails closed both ways. The guard's step-down proof reads no clock: a new guard record file. The loop gate writes the time in loop-start.json, a label: the guard tells the loops apart by pid
the window events reads when no --since is given, and when -f stops for --until: a step shows more or fewer events, and removes nothing
the start time on an image pull's op record: a label
the timings' now, --since back from now, how long a live job has run, which queued lines are fresh, and when a stop was asked: display and labels
moved from cli.ts: the now the logins screen counts back from: display
the now --since and --until count back from: which lines to show
whether the temporary admin SSH window is open, for the policy printed: a step moves its end by the step, and the check row warns while it is open
the start time on a selftest run's op record: a label
moved from cli.ts: the now for status's recent-logins line: display; whether the temporary admin SSH window is open: display. The move to v3 is shown for a day once proved: a label
when a tool refresh was asked, and how long the command watches it: a step only stops watching sooner or later, and the refresh carries on

the guard's answer to a confirm: pending.ts judges each item by wall, boot and monotonic clock together, so a step either way lapses it; and the id of the event that names the admin in root's record: a label
the code wait's end when the op has no deadline: the op's record ends the wait first
when a connect began, and the waits for GitHub, a code and the keeping phase: a step only ends a wait, which changes nothing and says so
the time on box install's own event log lines: labels
how long the controller watches a connect it began: the op carries on at the box whatever a step does, and the polls are counted too

the time on an envelope the controller makes, a signed statement's time (the box judges its 5 minutes), a claim proof's time, which the box takes within 5 minutes of its own clock and only once, by its counter, and when a status was read: display
a temp file's unique name
a statement's time, which the box judges within 5 minutes, and the controller's own waits: a step only ends a wait
the controller's Clock, and the time on its own envelopes and events: labels; the time on a flow's one --json envelope: a label
when a box was first not reached, when each note was last said, and the hold lease's times: a step only moves when a note is said again
when a box was paired, and the time on the controller's events: labels
the time a trial's result is recorded: a label
when the controller last looked for an update, and the time on its events: a step only looks sooner or later
an op's end time and spawn time, and the 30 s a new job has to take its lease: a step only changes that grace; a free lease is the proof. Op deadlines are on mono
a request's 2 minutes and a signed statement's 5 minutes: times another machine wrote, which only the wall clock can judge; the nonce is what makes a signature work once
an event's time and id, and the minute windows of its rate limits: a step only shortens or lengthens a window
when each guard pass starts and ends: a pass's timing for its row
a stale temp name in a spool (removing it early costs a resend) and the spool pass's time budget (a step leaves requests for the next pass)
the workspaces gate's now: the state must be within 3 minutes either way, so a step fails closed
a GitHub App JWT's iat, for the loop and connect, the offset GitHub reports, and a failure's time for a status line
the guard record's time, its full pass timer, and the freshness readers check (a stale record fails closed). A VM start judges a loss by mono and the boot too
a beat's wall time and a log line's time, for people to read only: every age is judged on mono
network diagnostics: the netwatch record's age, a job's window end and the detail files' age; nothing but a diagnostics file past keepDays is removed on it
installedAt labels, the lock's time, and the wait for Tailscale to start: a step only waits less or more
when a stop was asked: a label in the stop's file
a rotation's deadline when its record has none: the guard ends the child on mono time
when an op began, a listener's minutes and a key's age: labels, and a wait the op's mono deadline bounds
an op's start, its deadline and a refused op's end: the child's limit runs on mono time (child.ts)
when an App was retired, a label, and the code wait: a step only ends a wait
a GitHub App JWT's iat and the clock offset GitHub reports: GitHub judges the JWT

the scheduler's now: when slots became ready or busy, an idle VM's turn, and when a VM was told to give way: a step only reorders a choice, gives an idle VM's turn away or ends a wait for a VM to go; no running job is ended
load status, load stop and load report: now for a session's labels, the source's freshness and the report's end: display only
a log line's time label

the loop's labels, beats, timers and state times for screens, pull and peer waits, give-way and sampling timers. Job ceilings and vmMaxHours are on mono alone, the drain on the boot uuid, and a VM start's loss on mono and the wall clock both. A forced stop's mark time, a label. Whether a test job's load session is still on: a step at worst ends a test job early, never a real one. An asked selftest's or pull's op times and a run's length: labels.
how long a selftest run or image pull's command watches before its --timeout: the op carries on whatever a step does
a restart record's time label, and vmStarting, which only puts off a one-time move of Softnet for a loop older than v2.5.1 while a VM starts. Whether a beat has gone quiet is judged on mono alone
the rollback watch's deadline and the proof's start: the watch file holds wall times, as v2.6.1's watcher reads them; the proof's own waits are on mono; the update lock's time, as v2.6.1 writes it
loop-start.json's time, a label: the guard tells v3's loop from v2.6.1's by pid

the rollback clock: v2.6.1's watcher compares the watch file's wall times with its own wall clock, so the pause is written in them, capped at placedAt plus 3 hours; the journal's step times are labels
when the selftest compared taskbox's rules with Softnet: the row's time label
netparse's hello and beat lines and its pruning: only its own rings past keepDays go on it
netwatch's tick: its record's age, the day's gap count and how old the pf reading is; nothing is removed or accepted on it
op list --since: a duration back from now, which only shows more or fewer records; and a loop op's cancel time, a label

screens and log reads, the undo's lock time, a pin's label, the hourly line for an unreadable watch, and the rollback watch's wall time: decideWatch uses it only for a watch with no mono count (v2.6.1's, or a clock it can't read), capped at 3 h. Remove's op record takes its start, end and phase times from it, for people to read; no deadline or lapse rests on them. A stale or stopped remove's end time, and the update lock's note of when remove took it, too. The workspaces block's now in status: display Whether the temporary admin SSH window is open, for status --json: display.. status shows the move to v3 for a day once proved: a label
the time label on a control.json written again as paused
the wall part of a Moment: a pending change and an outcome lapse on the wall clock too, and mono and the boot hold them to their limits
the journal's start, a label, and the starts in the last hour, a bound that only makes the move wait

a statement's 5 minutes and a request's time when the spool is over its cap, and a dropped request's outcome time: times another machine wrote, or a label; nothing is removed by it but what the spool's cap already removes
when the settings repo was last read, for the hourly read: a step only moves the next read
the update window is the box's own wall time, as the owner sets it, and the hourly look at a signer change: a step moves the window or the next look, never a limit
the logins keeper's minute: a timer

the time on the guard's record of starts when it changes, a lock file's age, and the id of an event made before the admin's entry that names it: a step only makes a lock look stale or fresh sooner, the record's order is its sequence number, and an id's time is a label
a progress record's updatedAt and its rate: display
when the queue was read and a run's queued time when GitHub gives none: the scheduler's order; a refusal's time, for its clock offset and a rate limit's wait when GitHub sends no Date
whether the temporary admin SSH window is open, for the rules compared: display
how old the keeper's counts file is, for a WARN row: display
the guard's record's freshness: a stale read FAILs, so a step fails closed
how long a retired App is listed, and each key's age for the Keys row: a step only shows it a little longer or shorter
whether netwatch's record is fresh, for the Network diagnostics row only
how long since the settings repo was read, and whether the temporary admin SSH window is open: display
when update --check asked for the read, so only a problem from that read is said: display
the time of a settings read, an op's phases and the settings in force: records and display; confirm's lapse uses the monotonic clock and the boot
the settings op's now, and the wall part of a confirm's moment, judged with the monotonic clock and the boot (pending.ts)
the agent shell's refusal envelope's at: a label
the bake's wait for its guest to shut down, and the base record's time: a step only ends a wait sooner or later, and the time is a label
a baking slot's beat and times, as every slot's are written, and a refresh op's end time: labels and beats
when the store's hashes were last checked and when a failed fetch or bake is tried again: a step only checks sooner or later
the waits for the sign-in and for the box to be online: a step only ends a wait sooner or later

labels in the install record, the marks and the watch file (whose placedAt and deadline v2.6.1's watcher reads; v3's counts mono), the deadline put on the monotonic clock's scale and moved later within the watch's cap, and whether a job or a proof came after the swap
the 7-day line about the release check, for display
the update window for a settings commit is the box's own wall time: a step moves the window, never a limit
when an admin's yes for a signer removal was given: the record's label; the 7-day wait is judged by signers.ts on the time it was first seen
the watch screen's now: display
a JWT, and whether the hourly workflows check and the last run are recent: a row's SKIP and display
the memory caps' 60 s over the size, on the guard's 2 s tick: a step forward asks a save or warns a minute early, a step back late; the stop at 150% reads no clock
workspace clear's name for the folder moved aside: unique by a counter, so a step only renames it

the workspace commands' now: freshness and quiet shown in list and status (display), and wait's --timeout, which gives up and changes nothing; a claim proof's time, which the box takes within 5 minutes of its own clock and only once, by its counter; rule list's live or expired, display
the moved-aside folder's name, from the caller's now: unique by a counter, so a step only renames it
the workspaces pass's now: its beat, the time rules (expiry, quiet, saves) and a failed proof's retry, all timers either way of a step; and when a clear's delete ended, for its op record
